name: MonarchAudioLevelMeter
title: AudioLevelMeter
summary: Shows how loud a microphone is, as rising segments or a thin bar, from a level the app measures.
whenToUse: In a call tile, a pre-call check or a recorder, to show that the microphone picks up sound.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a recording or an upload, use ProgressView. For a waveform over time, draw one from the samples.
api: MonarchAudioLevelMeter.init(_ level: Double, label: String? = nil, variant: MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant = .segments, size: MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize = .md, segments: Int = 5, isMuted: Bool = false, mutedLabel: String? = nil, isDecorative: Bool = false)

options.name: level
options.description: The loudness, 0 through 1. Values outside are limited to that range.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Microphone level".

options.name: variant
options.description: segments are rising bars the size of a word; bar is one thin bar that fills the width.

options.name: size
options.description: sm (12 points high) or md (16). Segments only.

options.name: segments
options.description: The number of segments. At least one.

options.name: isMuted
options.description: The microphone is off: the meter is empty and reads "Muted".

options.name: isDecorative
options.description: Hides the meter from assistive technology.

states.name: silent
states.description: Every segment is a dot in the strong border colour; the bar is an empty track.

states.name: sound
states.description: Segments up to the level are tall and in the success colour; the bar is filled to the level.

states.name: muted
states.description: Empty, in the disabled colours, and read as "Muted".

states.name: reduce motion
states.description: The meter does not follow the level: it is full at or above a level of 0.08 and empty below.

appearance: Segments that are on use the success solid colour and those that are off the strong border colour; the bar's track is the muted background. A muted meter uses the disabled text colour and the muted background, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web component can measure a MediaStream itself with the Web Audio API; on iOS capturing audio needs the microphone permission and an audio session, which belong to the app, so the meter only takes a level. On the web a segment that is off keeps its height and changes colour; here it is drawn as a dot, so the level can be read without colour. The web variants bars and bar are named segments and bar. The meter scales with Dynamic Type. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The meter is one element named "Microphone level" (or label) whose value is the level as a whole percentage in the user's locale, or "Muted".
It has the updates-frequently trait, so VoiceOver does not read every change.
With Reduce Motion the meter shows only whether there is sound; the spoken value is still the real level.
Segments that are on are tall and segments that are off are dots, so the level does not depend on colour.
isDecorative hides it when the same information is given elsewhere.
The segments rise towards the trailing side and the bar fills from the leading edge, in both layout directions.
edgeCases: A level that is not finite is treated as silence.
A segment count below one draws one segment.
The level changes without animation; pass a smoothed level for a calmer meter.
The meter is not interactive and has no touch target.

examples.title: A bar, muted
examples.setup:
@State private var level = 0.6
@State private var isMuted = true

parityExceptions.reason: The web example is an animated meter with no text, tone or button, so there is no scenario to pin.
parityExceptions.convention: Both native components keep their own examples.
